module_title: Budget Structure - Revenue vs. Capital Accounts
introduction: To understand the budget, you must distinguish between Revenue (Recurring) and Capital (Asset-forming) accounts. This level focuses on which money changes the government's 'Balance Sheet' and which does not.

core_concepts.title: Revenue Budget (The Operational Account)
core_concepts.description:
Includes items that do NOT impact the government's Assets or Liabilities. 
- Revenue Receipts: Tax (GST, Income Tax) and Non-Tax (Interest, Dividends). 
- Revenue Expenditure: Salaries, Pensions, Subsidies, and Interest Payments on old loans.

core_concepts.title: Capital Budget (The Investment Account)
core_concepts.description:
Includes items that CHANGE the government's Assets or Liabilities. 
- Capital Receipts: Borrowings (Liability increases), Disinvestment (Asset decreases), Recovery of loans. 
- Capital Expenditure: Building roads, bridges, hospitals (Asset increases), and Repayment of loans (Liability decreases).

core_concepts.title: The Significance of Capex
core_concepts.description: Revenue expenditure is like 'consumption' (money spent and gone), whereas Capital Expenditure (Capex) is like 'investment'. A healthy economy tries to increase the share of Capex because it builds productive capacity for the future.

important_entities.name: Disinvestment
important_entities.significance: When the government sells its shares in PSUs (like LIC or Air India), it is called disinvestment. Since it reduces the government's assets, it is categorized as a 'Capital Receipt'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume interest payments are 'Capital' because they relate to loans. WRONG. Repaying the principal amount is Capital, but paying the 'Interest' is a recurring expense and thus falls under 'Revenue Expenditure'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Capital changes the Balance Sheet; Revenue runs the office.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If the transaction creates an asset or reduces a loan, it's Capital. Otherwise, it's Revenue.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC often lists items and asks which are Revenue Expenditures. Remember: 'Interest Payments' is usually the single largest item of Revenue Expenditure in the Indian budget.
